passage: Biologist Priya Natarajan hypothesized that a species of desert lizard regulates its body temperature by changing color: darkening in cool mornings to absorb heat and lightening at midday to reflect it.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Natarajan's hypothesis?
choices: Lizards kept in enclosures at constant temperatures throughout the day showed little change in color.
Lizards of this species are darker in color than most other lizard species living in the same desert.
Lizards of this species spend more time in the shade at midday than in the early morning.
Lizards of this species change color more often during the breeding season than at other times.
steps: The hypothesis links color change to temperature control.
If temperature is constant and color stops changing, color change depends on temperature, which supports her.
Comparing with other species, shade-seeking behavior or breeding-season changes doesn't connect color to temperature regulation.
key: Supporting evidence should test the exact cause-and-effect the hypothesis proposes.
